findings.reason: the plan must extend `roadmap.implementable_sections` with the landing subtraction (or name in its text why that owner cannot carry the question) instead of minting a parallel reader.
findings.text: §18 claims "only two readers answer which sections are still work" and hoists `promotion._plan_remaining_sections` to a new public name on `reckon/_store.py`, but `roadmap.implementable_sections` (reckon/roadmap.py:106) is a public reader of the same declaration map answering the same declared-implementable question (it returns every section classified `implementable`, differing from promotion's only by the landing subtraction), and it is the reader consumed by `reckon/roadmap.py:2939`, `reckon/mcp_views.py:3379` and `reckon/crew/runs.py:1486`; a fresh public reader in the store would be the third public answer to one question

findings.reason: the plan must either state that the slug normalisation and `_top` fallback are dropped deliberately, or extend the owning derivation with the fallback rather than deleting a reader whose output differs.
findings.text: §16 asserts `evidence._section_key` "derives the identical key from the same inputs with a slug fallback" and deletes it in favour of `section_record_id`, but they diverge for inputs evidence actually groups by: `_section_key("a / b")` is `"a-b"` while `section_record_id("a / b")` is `"a / b"`, and `_section_key("")` is `"_top"` while `section_record_id("")` is `""`, so the deletion is not behaviour-preserving for slug sections or the empty/`_top` bucket evidence uses at reckon/evidence.py:69 and :336

findings.reason: the plan should route `normalize_section` through a derivation that returns its canonical dotted spelling (its own capture, or a hoisted `section_record_id` that preserves the dotted form) rather than through a candidate set that has already discarded that information.
findings.text: §16 says `ledger.normalize_section` keeps its name and output but "derives it through `section_id_candidates`", yet `section_id_candidates` returns an unordered set of address spellings (`section_id_candidates("5.1")` = `{"5.1","s5-1","s5.1"}`) with no `§`-prefixed element, and `normalize_section("5.1")` must return `"§5.1"`, which is in no candidate set for any input, so the asserted reuse cannot reproduce the label

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §16 hides the per-section digest set, the three recognised fingerprint forms and the coverage predicate behind the unchanged `plan_fingerprint` public signature plus one module-private function; §17 and §18 hoist existing recognisers and readers rather than splitting them into parallel wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §18 hoists promotion's outstanding-sections reader to a new public name on `reckon/_store.py` while `roadmap.implementable_sections` already publicly answers the declared-implementable question and is the reader the roadmap/MCP/crew surfaces consume.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1476, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16 names the `legacy` flag it retires and the two public names its hoist moves (net zero), §17 names `landed_section_ids` moved under its own name and its retired private heading walks (net one, `plan_headings`), and §18 names its private promotion name retired in favour of one public store reader (net one), so each section accounts for its surface.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites much existing machinery, but two of its claimed reuses fail against the code: §16's `evidence._section_key` is not "identical" to `section_record_id`, and §16's `ledger.normalize_section` cannot derive its output through `section_id_candidates`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the one genuinely new public reader, `plan_headings` on `reckon/_plan_html.py`, exposes an extended private parser's yield and the plan states why `structured_section_spans` keeps its spans-only contract, so no layer is added without a reason it cannot extend the machinery beneath it.
